outcomes: A run that may publish knows its bound commit's ancestry and holds its publish credential before any repository code runs
A bound request without invocation.publication only gates: it plans no publication and starts no publication provider
A run whose credential provider negotiates publication-v1 resolves, opens, uploads and releases through that one session, and no repository process holds a publish credential
nonGoals: Uploading a member of an ecosystem other than npm, Go modules and OCI images under publication-v1; such a plan is refused before it opens
Publishing a bound request through publication-v1; its expected plan names no open or upload node, so the executing engine refuses the plan it builds

requirements.text: A run naming publish or deploy, or a bound request with invocation.publication, reads its bound commit's ancestry into memory at process start, before the first-use bootstrap, an install or the first hook: PUTNAMI_SOURCE_REVISION, else HEAD, ignoring replace refs, grafts and the commit-graph, so later writes change no answer. The engine run reuses that snapshot. It names a shallow clone; above 1,000,000 commits it holds a named error and no commit. Other runs read none. With publish enabled, the credential provider starts before the first hook, locally as on a hosted run.

A bound request without invocation.publication enables no publish purpose, even when its invocation.providers names publish, and says so on stderr. When its plan holds a task of a publication command or with declared registry or cloud effects, or its versions start a release-set publication, the executing engine refuses it before any release-set or deploy provider starts. A gate-only request plans no publish job and starts no release-set provider.

The engine offers publication-v1 at initialize and uses it only when the credential provider echoes it; without the echo the existing release-set path runs unchanged. With it, the provider resolves the channels and no release-set provider process starts. One open node waits for the bound request's barrier commands, or, locally, for every task that neither publishes nor depends on one, and sends the plan digest, the channel heads and the ancestry snapshot. The provider refuses a second plan in one session and a head that is not an ancestor of the bound commit. Release sends the published artifacts, the heads it moves from, the ancestry and the evidence. Open and release are retried once, on a transport error only, and a release is idempotent by plan digest. A refusal is a bounded error that names its code, and moves no channel. A local run and a hosted run of one commit open the same plan and release the same set.

Under publication-v1 each publication job receives a private outbox, PUTNAMI_PUBLICATION_OUTBOX with mode 0700, and no registry or cloud credential, credential descriptor or registry route. One upload node per publication job runs in the engine after the job and the open. It hashes every outbox file again, refuses a member the plan does not select, or a version or project the plan does not assign, asks the provider for the publish credential of the member's registry, and uploads the npm tarball, Go module zip or OCI layout in process. It records published-image.json for an OCI member and reports one published-member event per upload. A job that wrote no descriptor packed nothing, and its node uploads nothing. A publication job whose result was reused instead of executed packed nothing in the run, and the release refuses.
